text:
Alice M.: Quick check — hitting a weird scoping issue when using service account impersonation + OIDC flow in the Node client. Token audience ends up as the impersonated account instead of my app client_id. Anyone seen this?
Ben K.: hmm. are you calling the token endpoint directly or using the SDK helper?
Alice M.: Using our Node SDK wrapper (redwood-sdk-auth). Code: 
```js
const client = new RedwoodAuth({impersonate: 'projects/123/serviceAccounts/sa-foo@proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com', oidcClientId: 'my-app-client'});
await client.getIdToken();
```
But the returned id_token 'aud' claim === 'sa-foo@...' not 'my-app-client'.
Carla R.: If you impersonate via STS exchange, the issued token audience can default to the impersonated service account unless you pass the OIDC target_audience param in the exchange. Are we doing STS under the hood?
Alice M.: I think so. The SDK does an impersonateCredentials().getIdToken() call. I assumed that would honor oidcClientId.
Samir P.: SDK implementation note: Google IAM impersonation -> generateIdToken has a target_audience arg, but the cloud STS flow (token exchange) sometimes returns a subject-audience tied to the SA if you skip the explicit target_audience. We had a bug where the Node helper didn't forward target_audience in the STS request.
Morgan L.: quick workaround: call generateIdToken on the impersonated account with the target_audience set, e.g. via REST: 
```bash
curl -X POST "https://iamcredentials.googleapis.com/v1/projects/-/serviceAccounts/sa-foo@proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com:generateIdToken" \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $IMPERSONATOR_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
 -d '{"audience":"my-app-client","includeEmail":true}'
```
Carla R.: also check if your code is using `scope` vs `audience`. For id tokens the audience is explicit via `audience`/`target_audience`, scopes don't apply.
Alice M.: Ah — the SDK was using getAccessToken() then exchanging via STS without passing audience. So that explains it. Any risks with doing generateIdToken on the SA directly?
Ben K.: You need IAM iam.serviceAccounts.getToken / serviceAccountTokenCreator role on the impersonator principal. Also watch quota and frequency — id token generation is rate-limited.
infra-bot: Reminder: internal doc -> https://playbooks.redwood.ai/auth/impersonation (last updated 2025-11-02) :thumbsup:
Samir P.: If you want to centralize, we can add an option to the SDK to forward `target_audience` through the STS call. Quick patch: add {target_audience: opts.oidcClientId} to the token exchange payload.
Morgan L.: Note for streaming clients: when using SSH/wss streaming, we saw reconnection flaps if tokens expire and refresh happens during in-flight frames. Make sure your streaming layer lets the auth header be swapped without tearing the socket unless the backend requires re-auth.
Alice M.: Good call. This is not streaming but planning ahead. For Node we likely should patch the helper. Samir — want me to open a PR with a failing test?
Samir P.: Yes please. Repro steps: 1) mock impersonation response; 2) call sdk.getIdToken({oidcClientId}) and assert aud claim in decoded token equals the client id. Use nock to intercept STS if needed.
Carla R.: If anyone running into cross-project scope, remember service account email vs numeric project id in impersonation path matters. Use `projects/-/serviceAccounts/` for org-level SAs. Otherwise the IAM API may return 403.
Ben K.: Also watch for concurrent refresh bug we found in Go SDK — two concurrent calls to getIdToken could race and both call IAM -> exhausted quota. We fixed it with an in-flight singleflight dedupe. Might be worth copying here.
Alice M.: Great — I'll open a PR with tests + mention singleflight for concurrency. Thanks all.
Ben K.: ping me in review, will sanity-check RBAC in the change.
Carla R.: +1. If you want I'll add a note to the auth troubleshooting doc about the audience vs impersonation quirk.
Alice M.: Thanks!
Morgan L.: quick TL;DR for future readers: impersonation + OIDC -> always pass explicit audience/target_audience during token generation/exchange; prefer generateIdToken on the impersonated SA when possible; guard refresh concurrency in client libs. :rocket:
